id: UX-02 Chrome recipient-key and HPKE local probe
scope: Two isolated Chrome profiles with the same test-only MetaMask EOA. This amends the older Firefox plan after the user removed Firefox from initial scope.
question: Does the actual MetaMask signature reproduce a recipient public key and decrypt a v1 HPKE receipt in a separate Chrome profile without transferring a secret key?

fixedBytes.personalSignMessage: The exact UTF-8 bytes are constructed by signature-probe.html: six newline-separated lines, no trailing newline; purpose ecu/uniswap/key-root/v1; decimal chainId; lowercase hex Pool and owner. This probe reuses that text unchanged.
fixedBytes.signature: 65 bytes r||s||v decoded from 0x-prefixed personal_sign hex. Require canonical low-s and v=27 or 28; recover address from EIP-191 hash of the exact message and require owner match. No byte rewrite before HKDF.
fixedBytes.hkdfOutput: 32-byte IKM for RFC 9180 DHKEM DeriveKeyPair, not a raw X25519 scalar. The 32-byte derived IKM and private key remain in memory only.
fixedBytes.hpkeInfo: D-08 info_i = Keccak-256(abi.encode(tag(ecu/hpke-info/v1), uint256 chainId, address pool, uint8 kind=1, bytes32 random salt, uint256 outputIndex=0, address owner, uint256 Cx=1, uint256 Cy=2, uint8 receiptFormat=1)). C=(1,2) is a valid curve point used only as a synthetic context; it is not derived from the receipt.
fixedBytes.plaintext: v||r, unsigned 32-byte big-endian each. Fresh random v in [1, 2^64] and r in [0, BN254 q) generated in profile A memory only.
fixedBytes.packet: enc (32 bytes) || ciphertext (80 bytes), 112 bytes total, hex encoded for manual public transfer

method: Build a local bundle from exact npm-locked dependencies, host it on 127.0.0.1, and obtain personal_sign from the real MetaMask extension in each profile.
Profile A derives the public recipient key and encrypts one synthetic receipt. Copy only the public envelope into profile B.
Profile B derives the key, checks owner/chain/pool match and public key equality, decrypts the packet, validates exact length and v/r ranges, and confirms a one-byte ciphertext tamper is rejected.
Run a local mock-wallet signature test of deterministic keys, independent receiver, expected packet lengths and tamper rejection before manual use.
passCriteria: Actual test-only MetaMask provides the same recipient public key in both independent Chrome profiles for the same chain, Pool and owner.
Profile B accepts an A-created 112-byte packet and rejects its one-byte tampering.
evidenceBoundary: No actual BN254 commitment equality, RecipientInfo EIP-712 signature, on-chain event or finalized/unspent history is tested. A success is a partial UX-02 result, not full recipient acceptance. No real funds are involved.
sensitiveDataRule: Never display, log, store or transmit raw signature, HKDF output, private key, plaintext amount, blinding, or seed. Only the public recipient key and public HPKE envelope may be copied.
